bodies.linkedin:
Table-aware ingestion decreased recall@5 by −0.067 in our RAG pipeline, proving that qualitative impressions of system performance are often wrong.

Most tutorial projects skip the golden-question evaluation harness, but we doubled our set from 30 to 60 questions to ensure candidate changes were not hidden by statistical noise. This rigor revealed that hybrid retrieval using dense embeddings and keyword indexing provided the largest single performance improvement, increasing recall@5 by +0.133.

We discovered that pdfplumber frequently merges words into single tokens, causing failures in FTS5 tokenization. All-lowercase welds represent 10.2% of all alphabetic tokens, rendering BM25 structurally blind to company-name queries. Query rewriting cannot fix issues where tokens are welded together in a way that prevents matching.

Our final optimized pipeline achieved a recall@5 of 0.733. We kept the bge-reranker-base model as the default because the large model's 45-second per-query latency on CPU is unacceptable for a product. 

Measure your retrieval quality with numbers, not vibes.

bodies.thread:
Table-aware ingestion decreased recall@5 by -0.067. Most RAG projects ship these features on faith, but measuring against a golden set proves when your intuition is wrong.

The initial 30-question evaluation set incorrectly suggested that query rewriting was the least valuable change, while the 60-question set revealed it as a critical failure mode.

Measurement bugs, such as false hits from stripping whitespace and false misses from misinterpreting commas, can lead to inaccurate evaluation of retrieval systems.

The pdfplumber tool frequently merges words together into single tokens, which causes failures in FTS5 tokenization. BM25 retrieval was structurally blind to company-name queries in holdings-table rows because of welded tokens.

Hybrid retrieval using dense embeddings and keyword indexing provided the largest single performance improvement. It increased recall@5 by +0.133.

RAG systems should prioritize the inclusion of a golden-question evaluation harness to objectively measure retrieval quality rather than relying on qualitative impressions.
